messages.content: "在一個物理實驗中，你被給予兩個電荷。第一個電荷的大小為5庫倫，第二個電荷的大小為10庫倫。這些電荷相距2公尺。你被要求計算這些電荷之間的電磁力。你進行了兩次實驗。第一次，電荷被放置在真空中，其介電常數為8.854 x 10^-12 F/m。第二次，電荷被放置在一個相對介電常數為5 x 10^-12 F/m的介質中。你能計算出兩種情況下電荷之間的電磁力嗎？"

function.name: electromagnetic_force
function.description: Calculate the electromagnetic force between two charges placed at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge1.description: The magnitude of the first charge in coulombs.

charge2.description: The magnitude of the second charge in coulombs.

distance.description: The distance between the two charges in meters.

medium_permittivity.description: The relative permittivity of the medium in which the charges are present. Default is 8.854 x 10^-12 F/m (vacuum permittivity). This is a float type value.

The user asks: "In a physics experiment, you have two charges: first charge magnitude 5 C, second 10 C, separated by 2 m. Compute the electromagnetic force between them. Two experiments: first in vacuum with permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m; second in a medium with relative permittivity 5e-12 F/m." Wait relative permittivity? They say "相對介電常數為5 x 10^-12 F/m". That seems wrong: relative permittivity is dimensionless. But they gave numeric value 5 x 10^-12 F/m, maybe they mean absolute permittivity? Actually they wrote "相對介電常數為5 x 10^-12 F/m", but relative permittivity should be dimensionless. Maybe it's a mistake and they meant absolute permittivity of the medium is 5 x 10^-12 F/m. So we need to compute Coulomb's law: F = k * q1 * q2 / r^2 where k = 1/(4π ε0) if using vacuum permittivity. If medium has permittivity ε, then k = 1/(4π ε). So we can use the function electromagnetic_force.

We need to call the function twice: once with default medium_permittivity (which defaults to 8.854e-12), and once with medium_permittivity=5e-12.

But note: The function signature expects medium_permittivity as optional number. We pass it accordingly.
